summary: Proof of concept E0 (proposal r22, H8) on synthetic bags, run on Kaggle CPU at the declared scale (gate 0: 6 configurations x 5 seeds; arms: 10 seeds x 3 trained arms x 2 strengths, up to 400 epochs). It replaces the r12 proof of concept (E1 on E-DAIC, all arms at chance), whose record stays in Results/E1_full.md and git history. Gate 0 passed (1.2199 vs constant 1.2642). P1, P2 and P4 are supported under the pre-registered rules, so H8 is carried forward, but the margins are thin: P1 and P2a both sit at Holm-adjusted p 0.0488, the bootstrap interval of the P2a mean difference crosses zero, and the per-item Spearman between the surrogate and the prompt prior is near zero for every arm, so the surrogate-error gain reads as shrinkage toward the prior rather than recovery of it. P3: removing text at inference costs 0.116 SS^w [0.071, 0.163]; the full model keeps about 17% of the r12 reference skill.

metrics.name: SS^w (Ec. 93) on test bags
metrics.why: Primary endpoint of H5 and the score H8 reads against the untargeted arm.

metrics.name: Surrogate error ||Rhat_c - Rc||_F^2 / (8 N_b) on test bags
metrics.why: The quantity the Ec. 77 penalty minimizes; separates a better profile from a better surrogate.

metrics.name: Subject-level AUROC of the summed item profile

hypotheses.statement: The full model has a class-weighted skill score above zero at rho = 0.5.
hypotheses.test: One-sample Wilcoxon (greater), seed as unit, n = 10, Holm over P1, P2a, P2b
hypotheses.observed: Mean 0.0244 (sd 0.0316); W = 45, raw p 0.0420, adjusted p 0.0488; rank-biserial 0.636; bootstrap CI [0.0038, 0.0401].
hypotheses.rationale: Adjusted p is below alpha, by 0.0012; one of ten seeds is negative (-0.055). Supported under the rule, with a thin margin.

hypotheses.statement: The full model has a higher SS^w and a lower surrogate error than the untargeted arm at rho = 0.5.
hypotheses.test: Two paired Wilcoxon tests (P2a greater, P2b less), seed as unit, Holm over P1, P2a, P2b
hypotheses.criterion: Supported when both adjusted p < 0.05; partially supported when one passes.
hypotheses.rationale: Both tests pass after Holm. P2a is fragile: its adjusted p equals P1's at 0.0488 and the bootstrap interval of the mean difference includes zero. P2b is clear, but the near-zero per-item Spearman of every arm suggests the lower error comes from shrinking Rhat_c toward the low-variance Rc rather than from recovering the item identity.

hypotheses.statement: At rho = 0 the paired SS^w difference between the full and the untargeted arms has a bootstrap interval containing zero.
hypotheses.test: Percentile bootstrap (B = 10000) of the seed-mean paired difference
hypotheses.criterion: Supported when the interval contains zero.
hypotheses.rationale: The interval contains zero; the penalty adds no SS^w when the audio carries no prompt information. Absence of evidence with n = 10, not evidence of equivalence.

novelty.claim: Distilling the interviewer-prompt prior into acoustics, with text as training-only privileged information (pillar C3, r22), improves the item profile over the same model without the penalty and does nothing when the audio does not carry the prior.
novelty.rationale: The pre-registered ablation (full vs untargeted) and the negative control pass, so the existence proof holds on synthetic bags. But the SS^w gain is small (0.008) with an interval crossing zero, and the per-item Spearman shows no recovery of the prior even at rho = 0.5, so the mechanism the claim names is not demonstrated. The cost of removing text (P3) is large.

qualitative_not_applicable: The pre-registered per-item fidelity heatmap was not rendered as a figure; its numbers are in poc_e0.json (arms.*.spearman). Seed-mean per-item Spearman of Rhat_c vs Rc: full rho 0.5 0.0014 (sd 0.0115), untargeted rho 0.5 -0.0074, full rho 0 0.0033, untargeted rho 0 -0.0014; max |rho_s| 0.098. The full model is marginally above the untargeted arm at rho 0.5, but no arm shows structure, which fails the qualitative expectation that the full model recovers the prior.
limitations: Synthetic bags only; nothing here transfers to E-DAIC.
Generator variant deviates from experiments v05 (identity enters audio only through rho * p[z], shared severity direction, no prompt/audio disagreement); to be recorded in experiments v06.

Weak signal by construction: logistic decodability of z is about 0.23 at rho 0.5 (chance 0.125), and the prompt prior Rc has very low variance (0.03 one-hot plus noise), which makes surrogate error a weak proxy for recovery.
P1 and P2a pass with adjusted p 0.0488 over 10 seeds; a rerun with other seeds could flip them.
Convergence curves, fidelity heatmap and interval plots were not rendered as figures.
next_steps: Record the generator deviation and the E0 outcome in experiments v06 and align E1-E9 with r22.
Before E-DAIC, check why the surrogate does not recover the prior (Spearman near zero): verify the Spearman computation, and consider a rho or Rc-variance sweep.
Render the pre-registered figures from poc_e0.json (curves, per-item heatmap, paired-difference intervals).

contribution_type.why: E0-P1, E0-P2 and E0-P4 are supported only on synthetic bags, with E0-P1 and E0-P2a at adjusted p 0.0488 and novelty partially_justified: the training-only distillation idea is shown feasible at pilot scale, while the mechanism (prior recovery, per-item Spearman near zero) and any real-data benefit remain unshown.

General.why: A general ML contribution would need the gain on real data; E0 is synthetic and the SS^w gain is 0.008 with an interval crossing zero.

Theory.why: No theorem or formal guarantee is proved; E0 is an empirical existence check.

Use-Inspired.why: Motivated by depression screening from interviews, but no E-DAIC result supports the use case yet.

Concept & Feasibility.why: A pilot-scale synthetic proof that the penalty-trained surrogate helps when audio carries the prior and not otherwise (E0-P1, E0-P2, E0-P4).

Negative Results.why: The prior r12 E1 was at chance and E0 shows no prior recovery, but the central E0 verdicts are supported, so the findings are not primarily negative.
